To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
universities have to develop strategies to increase their international attractiveness as well as to strengthen regional networks.
universities have to develop a new strategy to strengthen their regional role as knowledge sources.

(1) universities are a key factor for regional knowledge management, (2) universities are a central factor for interregional co-operative knowledge networks, (3) universities have to strengthen and coordinate these two functions, and (4) this requires a strategic approach to the internationalisation process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research questions: How can universities strengthen their role in interregional knowledge management?
the following questions: - How do the strategies of universities to strengthen their interregional co-operations affect regional processes of generating and applying knowledge?
the following questions: How can the role of universities within regional knowledge networks be explained?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
universities have to be seen as a central actor in a transregional knowledge management.
universities have to develop their own internationalisation strategies in order to be able to react on the increasing interregional competition in the fields of education, research, and innovation.
universities have to be aware of the fact that the role they play within regional knowledge networks is changing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
universities have to be seen as a central element of regional innovation systems, but also as a central element in interregional knowledge management.
universities can contribute to interregional knowledge management in a twofold way.
the success of universities' internationalisation strategies depends on the existence of regional knowledge networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
universities can play a key role for the development of regional knowledge networks, but only if they are able to react to new challenges by developing and implementing suitable strategies.
internationalisation strategies of universities have to be coordinated carefully with regional knowledge management strategies.
universities are not only important actors in the regional knowledge networks, but that they also have to take care for their interregional dimension.
